title: A prayer to see virtues
hook: Rebbe Elimelech's prayer asks to see the virtues of others, not their faults
carry: pray to see others' virtues, not their faults
tomorrow: under all the layers, what's left that never got dirty?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Levi Yitzchak, the people's lawyer, beside Paul's love that thinketh no evil. Judge every person toward merit. Today closes the week, with a prayer that asks for new eyes.

A camera can pick one face out of a crowd in a blink. Picking out what's good in that face takes longer. Rabbi Elimelech of Lizhensk, the Hasidic master known as Rebbe Elimelech, wrote a short prayer to be said before the daily prayers, and yes, it asks exactly that. It's not a long prayer, and it isn't abstract. Among its requests: put it in our hearts that each of us sees the virtues of others, and not their faults.
screen: `A FACE IN A CROWD, IN A BLINK.` → `A PRAYER BEFORE PRAYER.` → `VIRTUES, NOT FAULTS.`

segments.voice: The prayer goes further than politeness. It asks that people speak with one another in a way that is upright before God, and that no hatred of one person for another rise in the heart. It's a request, not an order, and it's said in the plural: us, each of us, all of us together. Rebbe Elimelech seems to know you can't simply decide to see differently, so he asks for help. Faults are loud; they announce themselves. Virtues are often quiet, and you have to be looking for them. And notice where it sits: before the morning prayers, as if a person can't stand before God well while still keeping score on everyone else. Now the week that led here. A wrestler who wins because he comes glad. A rebbe hunting for one good point. An hour alone, in your own words. Seven beggars, each flaw opening on a gift. A son who waited too long. A rabbi who argued the people's case in heaven. And a prayer to see the virtues. Seven days of later voices, one thread running through them: look again, and look kindly, at others and at yourself.
screen: `NO HATRED IN THE HEART.` · `A REQUEST, NOT AN ORDER.` · `BEFORE YOU STAND BEFORE GOD.` · `ONE THREAD: LOOK AGAIN, KINDLY.` · then, large: `PRAY TO SEE OTHERS' VIRTUES, NOT THEIR FAULTS.`

segments.voice: Bring one person to mind, someone close or someone hard. Count their virtues on your fingers, slowly, one for each breath: a skill, a kindness, a way they show up. If the person is a hard one, the first virtue may take a while; let it. When you run out, start again from the first and see whether a new one comes.
See the virtues: from Rebbe Elimelech's prayer before prayer. Asking to see the good in others, and not their faults. The last word of the week.
Here it is, folded small: pray to see others' virtues, not their faults. Seven days of teachers in one request. A good week to you.
